subject.title: [Bug]: Google Chat: Space/Group messages silently ignored (DMs work correctly)

question: Should Google Chat HTTP-endpoint Space events treat any delivered `USER_MENTION` event as sufficient activation when exact `botUser` matching is unreliable, or should OpenClaw keep requiring exact app-user matching and solve this only with better setup/proof?
rationale: Source proves where the skip happens, but the safe permanent behavior depends on live Google Chat payload details and maintainer intent around mention-gating defaults for a channel where Google may only deliver mentioned Space messages.

options.title: Live-Prove And Fix Mention Detection
options.body: Capture a redacted current Space event payload, then update plugin-local mention detection and diagnostics so real @mentions create group sessions without disabling mention gating.

options.title: Consolidate Google Chat Space Routing
options.body: Move the remaining work into a single Google Chat Space/thread routing owner if maintainers want one canonical issue for ingress, mention, and thread metadata.

options.title: Document Explicit Workaround
options.body: Treat `requireMention:false` as the supported HTTP-endpoint Space mode only if maintainers intentionally accept that product behavior.

recommendation.title: Live-Prove And Fix Mention Detection
recommendation.body: Capture a redacted current Space event payload, then update plugin-local mention detection and diagnostics so real @mentions create group sessions without disabling mention gating.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history across the Google Chat access-policy and shared mention-gating code that controls this decision.
